title: Biomolecules
syllabus: Chemical constituents of living cells: Biomolecules - structure and function of proteins, carbohydrates, lipids, nucleic acids; Primary and secondary metabolites; Nature of bond linking monomers in a polymer; Dynamic state of body constituents - concept of metabolism; Metabolic basis for living; The living state; Enzymes - chemical nature, properties, mechanism of enzyme action, factors affecting enzyme activity, classification and nomenclature of enzymes, co-factors.

questions.question: When living tissue is ground with trichloroacetic acid ($\text{Cl}_3\text{CCOOH}$) and filtered, which of the following biomolecules is retrieved in the acid-insoluble fraction despite having a molecular weight not exceeding $800\text{ Da}$?
questions.solution: Lipids have molecular weights not exceeding $800\text{ Da}$. However, during tissue disruption, cell membranes fragment and form insoluble water-impermeable vesicles that do not filter through, ending up in the acid-insoluble retentate (macromolecular fraction).

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding categories of secondary metabolites and their representative examples:

List-I (Category)List-II (Example)
(A) Alkaloids(I) Concanavalin A
(B) Toxins(II) Morphine and Codeine
(C) Lectins(III) Abrin and Ricin
(D) Drugs(IV) Vinblastine and Curcumin

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Alkaloids: Morphine, Codeine; Toxins: Abrin, Ricin; Lectins: Concanavalin A; Drugs: Vinblastine, Curcumin; Pigments: Carotenoids, Anthocyanins; Terpenoids: Monoterpenes, Diterpenes.

questions.question: Which of the following is an amino acid with a neutral side chain and contains a hydroxymethyl group ($-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) as its variable R-group?
questions.solution: In amino acids: Glycine has $\text{R} = -\text{H}$; Alanine has $\text{R} = -\text{CH}_3$; Serine has $\text{R} = -\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ (hydroxymethyl group).

questions.question: The most abundant protein in the whole of the biosphere and the most abundant protein in the animal world are respectively:
questions.solution: Ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase-oxygenase (RuBisCO) is the most abundant protein in the whole biosphere, and Collagen is the most abundant protein in the animal world.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the levels of protein structure and their descriptive features:

List-I (Protein Structure)List-II (Defining Feature)
(A) Primary structure(I) Complex assembly of multiple polypeptide subunits (e.g., adult Hemoglobin: $2\alpha + 2\beta$)
(B) Secondary structure(II) Linear sequence of amino acids from N-terminal to C-terminal
(C) Tertiary structure(III) Local spatial folding forming right-handed $\alpha$-helices and $\beta$-pleated sheets
(D) Quaternary structure(IV) Hollow woolen ball-like 3D folding essential for biological and enzymatic activity

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Primary structure: Positional sequence of amino acids (first amino acid = N-terminal, last = C-terminal); Secondary: Local folding into $\alpha$-helix (only right-handed) or $\beta$-sheet; Tertiary: Complete 3D folding creating active sites; Quaternary: Spatial arrangement of multiple interacting polypeptide subunits.

questions.question: Lecithin is an important component of cell membranes. Chemically, it is classified as a:
questions.solution: Lecithin (phosphatidylcholine) is a phospholipid having glycerol esterified with two fatty acids, a phosphate group, and a choline nitrogenous base. It is a major constituent of cell membranes.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the types of chemical bonds and their occurrences in biomolecules:

List-I (Bond Type)List-II (Occurrence)
(A) Peptide bond(I) Links monosaccharide units in polysaccharides
(B) Glycosidic bond(II) Links adjacent amino acids in a polypeptide chain
(C) Phosphodiester bond(III) Formed between fatty acid carboxyl group and glycerol hydroxyl group
(D) Ester bond(IV) Links $3'$-carbon of one nucleotide to $5'$-carbon of next nucleotide in a nucleic acid

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Peptide bond: $-\text{CO}-\text{NH}-$ between amino acids; Glycosidic bond: Links sugars with dehydration; Phosphodiester bond: Links $3'-\text{OH}$ of one deoxyribose to $5'-\text{OH}$ of adjacent via phosphate; Ester bond: Connects fatty acids to glycerol.

questions.question: Which of the following is a NON-REDUCING disaccharide?
questions.solution: Sucrose is formed by linking $C_1$ of $\alpha$-D-glucose to $C_2$ of $\beta$-D-fructose. Since both potential free aldehyde/ketone reducing carbonyl groups are locked in the glycosidic bond, sucrose is non-reducing.

questions.question: Starch forms a deep blue helical complex with iodine ($\text{I}_2$), whereas cellulose does not give this color reaction because:
options: Starch forms helical secondary structures that can trap $\text{I}_2$ molecules, whereas cellulose lacks complex helices
Starch is a heteropolysaccharide of glucose and galactose
Cellulose is broken down instantly by iodine
questions.solution: Starch forms secondary helical structures where the amylose helical interior traps $\text{I}_2$ molecules to produce a blue-black color. Cellulose has rigid linear $\beta-1,4$ chains lacking helices and cannot hold iodine.

questions.question: Exoskeletons of arthropods (such as insects and crabs) and cell walls of fungi are made of the complex homopolysaccharide chitin, which is a polymer of:
questions.solution: Chitin is a linear nitrogen-containing structural homopolysaccharide composed of repeating units of N-acetylglucosamine (NAG) linked by $\beta-1,4$-glycosidic bonds.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the structures of Nucleosides, Nucleotides, and Nitrogenous Bases:

List-I (Compound)List-II (Chemical Nature / Identity)
(A) Adenine(I) Nucleotide (Adenosine + Phosphate)
(B) Adenosine(II) Heterocyclic purine nitrogenous base
(C) Adenylic acid(III) Nucleoside (Adenine + Ribose sugar)
(D) Uracil(IV) Pyrimidine nitrogenous base found only in RNA

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Adenine/Guanine: Purine bases; Uracil/Cytosine/Thymine: Pyrimidine bases; Adenosine/Uridine: Nucleosides (Base + Sugar); Adenylic acid/Uridylic acid: Nucleotides (Base + Sugar + Phosphate).

questions.question: According to the Watson-Crick B-DNA double-helix model, which of the following geometric parameters is INCORRECT?
options: The pitch of the helical turn is $3.4\text{ nm}$ with approximately 12 base pairs per turn.
The two polynucleotide strands run antiparallel ($5' \to 3'$ and $3' \to 5'$).
The distance between two consecutive base pairs is $0.34\text{ nm}$ ($3.4\text{ \AA}$).
Adenine pairs with Thymine via two hydrogen bonds ($\text{A}=\text{T}$) and Guanine pairs with Cytosine via three hydrogen bonds ($\text{G}\equiv\text{C}$).
questions.solution: In B-DNA, the pitch of the helix is $3.4\text{ nm}$ ($34\text{ \AA}$) and there are 10 base pairs in each complete turn (not 12), resulting in a distance of $0.34\text{ nm}$ between successive base pairs.

questions.question: Palmitic acid and Arachidonic acid contain how many total carbon atoms, including their carboxylic acid carbon?
questions.solution: Palmitic acid has 16 carbons including the carboxyl carbon [$\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_{14}\text{COOH}$]. Arachidonic acid is a polyunsaturated fatty acid containing 20 carbons including the carboxyl carbon.

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding the dynamic state of body constituents and metabolism:
Statement I: All living organisms exist in a non-equilibrium steady state to be able to perform work.
Statement II: The living state and metabolism are synonymous; without metabolism, there cannot be a living state.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Systems at equilibrium cannot perform work. Living organisms constantly consume energy to maintain a non-equilibrium steady state. Hence, the living state is a non-equilibrium steady-state maintained by continuous metabolic flux.

questions.question: How do biological enzymes accelerate the rate of chemical reactions?
options: By lowering the activation energy barrier of the transition state
By increasing the activation energy requirement
By altering the overall equilibrium constant of the reaction
By shifting the free energy change ($\Delta G$) of products
questions.solution: Enzymes lower the activation energy barrier needed to reach the high-energy unstable transition state, allowing substrate molecules to convert into products at much higher velocities without altering $\Delta G$ or the equilibrium constant.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the major classes of enzymes according to the IUBMB classification:

List-I (Enzyme Class)List-II (Type of Reaction Catalyzed)
(A) Oxidoreductases (Class 1)(I) Catalyze transfer of a group (other than hydrogen) between a pair of substrates
(B) Transferases (Class 2)(II) Catalyze oxidation-reduction between two substrates
(C) Hydrolases (Class 3)(III) Catalyze hydrolysis of ester, ether, peptide, or glycosidic bonds
(D) Lyases (Class 4)(IV) Catalyze removal of groups from substrates leaving double bonds without hydrolysis

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Class 1: Oxidoreductases/dehydrogenases; Class 2: Transferases; Class 3: Hydrolases; Class 4: Lyases (group removal leaving double bonds); Class 5: Isomerases; Class 6: Ligases (catalyze linking of two compounds with ATP breakdown).

questions.question: In competitive enzyme inhibition, a competitive inhibitor (e.g., malonate inhibiting succinate dehydrogenase):
options: Closely resembles the substrate in structure, binds to the active site, increases $K_m$, but leaves $V_{\text{max}}$ unchanged
Binds to an allosteric site, decreases both $K_m$ and $V_{\text{max}}$
Irreversibly destroys the enzyme protein, reducing $V_{\text{max}}$ without affecting $K_m$
questions.solution: Competitive inhibitors closely mimic substrate structure (e.g., malonate mimics succinate) and compete for the active site. Increasing substrate concentration overcomes inhibition; thus $V_{\text{max}}$ remains unchanged while apparent $K_m$ increases.

questions.question: A complete catalytically active conjugated enzyme consisting of a protein part combined with its non-protein cofactor is called a:
questions.solution:
$$\text{Holoenzyme} = \text{Apoenzyme (protein part)} + \text{Cofactor (non-protein part)}$$
If the cofactor is removed, the catalytic activity of the apoenzyme is lost.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the three distinct types of enzyme cofactors:

List-I (Cofactor Category)List-II (Specific Feature / Example)
(A) Prosthetic group(I) Tightly bound organic moiety permanently attached to apoenzyme (e.g., Haem in peroxidase)
(B) Coenzyme(II) Transiently bound organic compound, often derived from vitamins (e.g., NAD/NADP from Niacin)
(C) Metal ion cofactor(III) Forms coordination bonds with substrate and active site (e.g., $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ in Carboxypeptidase)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Prosthetic groups are tightly/permanently bound organic factors (e.g., Haem in peroxidase/catalase). Coenzymes are transient organic carriers often containing vitamins (NAD, NADP contain niacin). Metal ions form coordination complexes (e.g., $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ for carboxypeptidase).

questions.question: Which of the following is an essential vitamin component of the coenzymes Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide (NAD) and NADP?
questions.solution: The coenzymes NAD and NADP contain the vitamin niacin (nicotinic acid/vitamin $\text{B}_3$).

questions.question: The Michaelis constant ($K_m$) of an enzyme is mathematically defined as:
options: The substrate concentration at which reaction velocity reaches half of its maximum value ($\frac{1}{2}V_{\text{max}}$)
The maximum velocity achieved at saturating substrate levels
The inhibitor concentration required to cause 50% inhibition
The turnover number of enzyme per minute
questions.solution: $K_m$ (Michaelis-Menten constant) represents the substrate concentration $[S]$ at which the reaction velocity is half maximal ($V = V_{\text{max}} / 2$). A lower $K_m$ value indicates higher affinity of the enzyme for its substrate.

questions.question: Which of the following inorganic elements is present in the lowest percentage by weight in the human body?
questions.solution: In the human body: Oxygen = $65.0\%$, Carbon = $18.5\%$, Hydrogen = $0.5\%$, Nitrogen = $3.3\%$, Calcium = $1.5\%$, and Silicon is negligible ($< 0.1\%$ / trace amount).

questions.question: Zwitterionic form of an amino acid exists at a characteristic pH called its isoelectric point. In a zwitterion, the amino acid carries:
options: Both positive ($- \text{NH}_3^+$) and negative ($- \text{COO}^-$) charges simultaneously with a net charge of zero
questions.solution: At specific pH (isoelectric point), the basic amino group is protonated ($- \text{NH}_3^+$) and the acidic carboxyl group is ionized ($- \text{COO}^-$), existing as an internal dipolar dipolar ion (zwitterion) with net charge zero.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an essential basic amino acid possessing a positive charge at physiological pH?
questions.solution: Lysine, Arginine, and Histidine are basic amino acids carrying extra amino groups. Glutamic acid and Aspartic acid are acidic amino acids; Valine is a neutral amino acid.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding proteins and their physiological roles in living systems:

List-I (Protein)List-II (Physiological Role)
(A) GLUT-4(I) Intercellular ground substance
(B) Collagen(II) Enables glucose transport into cells
(C) Antibody(III) Fights infectious agents
(D) Trypsin(IV) Proteolytic digestive enzyme

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: GLUT-4: Enables insulin-mediated glucose transport across cells; Collagen: Intercellular ground substance; Antibody: Immunoglobulin fighting pathogens; Trypsin: Protein-digesting enzyme.

questions.question: Glycerol is a simple lipid constituent having the chemical formula of:
questions.solution: Glycerol is a simple trihydric alcohol with chemical name propane-1,2,3-triol (trihydroxy propane).

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding nucleic acid secondary structure is INCORRECT?
options: The backbones of DNA strands are formed by alternating heterocyclic bases and hydrogen bonds.
The sugar and phosphate form the structural backbone of the polynucleotide chain.
Nitrogenous bases project roughly perpendicular to the main axis pointing inwards.
The two strands of DNA are complementary to each other.
questions.solution: The structural backbone of DNA is formed by alternating sugar-phosphate-sugar units linked by phosphodiester bonds. The nitrogenous bases project inwards perpendicular to the backbone.

questions.question: Enzymes that catalyze the joining together of carbon-oxygen, carbon-sulfur, carbon-nitrogen, or phosphorus-oxygen bonds coupled with the cleavage of ATP belong to class:
questions.solution: Ligases (Class 6) catalyze the condensation linking of two molecules by forming $\text{C}-\text{O}, \text{C}-\text{S}, \text{C}-\text{N},$ or $\text{P}-\text{O}$ bonds with the simultaneous breakdown of ATP (e.g., DNA Ligase, Glutamine synthetase).

questions.question: Anabolic pathways differ from catabolic pathways because anabolic pathways:
options: Lead to more complex structures from simpler ones and consume energy (biosynthetic pathways)
Break complex molecules into simpler ones and release energy
questions.solution: Anabolic (biosynthetic) pathways synthesize complex molecules from simpler precursors and consume metabolic energy (e.g., protein synthesis from amino acids). Catabolic pathways degrade complex molecules into simpler ones, liberating energy (e.g., glycolysis).

questions.question: Gingelly oil (sesame oil) remains in liquid state during cold winter seasons because it contains:
options: Unsaturated fatty acids with lower melting points
Long-chain saturated fatty acids with high melting points
questions.solution: Oils (like gingelly oil) are rich in unsaturated fatty acids (containing one or more double bonds) which possess low melting points, allowing them to remain liquid during winters.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the percentage composition of cellular components in an average cell:

List-I (Component)List-II (% of Total Cellular Mass)
(A) Water(I) $10 - 15\%$
(B) Proteins(II) $70 - 90\%$
(C) Nucleic acids(III) $5 - 7\%$
(D) Lipids(IV) $2\%$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Water: $70-90\%$; Proteins: $10-15\%$; Nucleic acids: $5-7\%$; Carbohydrates: $3\%$; Lipids: $2\%$; Ions: $1\%$.

questions.question: In a polypeptide chain of 100 amino acids, how many peptide bonds are present?
questions.solution: Formation of a linear unbranched polymer of $n$ amino acids requires $(n - 1)$ dehydration condensation reactions. For 100 amino acids, there are $100 - 1 = 99$ peptide bonds.

questions.question: The curve showing the effect of temperature on enzyme activity is characteristically:
options: Bell-shaped (symmetrical parabola with an optimum temperature)
questions.solution: Enzyme activity is low at low temperatures (temporarily inactive), increases up to an optimum temperature, and then drops sharply due to heat denaturation of the enzyme protein, producing a characteristic bell-shaped curve.

questions.question: A competitive inhibitor of succinic dehydrogenase is:
questions.solution: Malonate closely resembles the substrate succinate in molecular structure and competitively inhibits succinic dehydrogenase in the Krebs cycle.

questions.question: Which of the following polysaccharides is stored inside animal liver and skeletal muscle cells as an instant reserve source of glucose?
questions.solution: Glycogen is a highly branched homopolymer of glucose stored in animal liver and muscle tissues. The right end of a glycogen chain is the reducing end and the left end is the non-reducing end.

questions.question: Inulin is a storage fructan polymer consisting of repeating monomer units of:
questions.solution: Inulin is a storage carbohydrate polymer found in Dahlia tubers consisting of repeating units of D-fructose.

questions.question: Zinc is an essential catalytic metal ion cofactor for which of the following proteolytic enzymes?
questions.solution: Zinc ($\text{Zn}^{2+}$) is a critical metal ion cofactor required for the catalytic activity of the proteolytic enzyme Carboxypeptidase and Carbonic anhydrase.

questions.question: Which of the following organic compounds is an aromatic amino acid?
questions.solution: Tyrosine, Phenylalanine, and Tryptophan contain aromatic carbon ring systems in their variable R side chains.

questions.question:
Read the following statements:
Statement I: Ribozymes are catalytic RNA molecules that act as biocatalysts without being proteins.
Statement II: Nucleic acids exhibit secondary structure through hydrogen bonding between complementary base pairs.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. Although almost all enzymes are proteins, there are catalytic RNA molecules called ribozymes (e.g., 23S rRNA). Nucleic acids also show secondary structure via complementary hydrogen bonding.

questions.question: The dynamic transition state structure of a substrate formed during an enzymatic reaction is:
options: Transient, highly unstable, and high in free energy
Stable and permanent with low energy
Identical in energy level to final products
questions.solution: During enzyme catalysis, the substrate binds to the active site to form an intermediate transition state complex ($ES^\ddagger$) that is temporary, highly unstable, and represents the peak energy barrier.

questions.question: The pitch of a single turn of the B-DNA double helix measures:
questions.solution: In B-DNA, each helical turn spans a distance (pitch) of $3.4\text{ nm}$ ($34\text{ \AA}$) containing 10 base pairs.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an essential polymeric substance categorized as a secondary metabolite with industrial applications?
questions.solution: Under secondary metabolites, Polymeric substances include Rubber, Gums, and Cellulose.

questions.question: In a saturated fatty acid, carbon atoms in the hydrocarbon chain are joined together by:
options: Only single covalent carbon-carbon bonds (no double bonds)
One or more carbon-carbon double bonds
questions.solution: Saturated fatty acids (like palmitic and stearic acid) contain only single carbon-carbon bonds ($\text{C}-\text{C}$), whereas unsaturated fatty acids contain one or more double bonds ($\text{C}=\text{C}$).

questions.question: The active site of an enzyme is defined as:
options: A specific pocket or crevice in the tertiary structure into which the substrate fits precisely
The N-terminal amino acid of the primary polypeptide chain
Any randomly exposed hydrophilic surface on the protein
questions.solution: The 3D folding of a protein's tertiary structure creates crevices or pockets called active sites, lined with catalytic amino acid side chains into which specific substrate molecules fit.

questions.question: Living organisms require a continuous input of free energy primarily because:
options: They constantly fight against reaching thermodynamic equilibrium (entropy death)
Enzymes decompose spontaneously at room temperature
Active transport decreases internal cell concentration to zero
questions.solution: Reaching thermodynamic equilibrium means zero free energy to do work, which corresponds to death. Organisms maintain continuous metabolic flux and energy input to stay in a non-equilibrium steady state.
